newsitem.title: USA: Fed coupon pass may be executed as early as Friday.
newsitem.headline: Fed coupon pass may be executed as early as Friday.

text.p: The Federal Reserve could execute a "coupon pass" -- market parlance for a permanent injection of funds into the banking system -- as early as Friday, economists said Monday.

"Since the last pass in early November was for bills, a coupon pass seems likely now. The Fed did not make a coupon pass in late November and this is why a large add need has built up earlier than usual this year and why a coupon pass that is frequently executed in mid-March or early April is likely to be advanced," said economists at MCM Moneywatch.

Economists at UBS Securities Inc said the Fed typically is forced to inject reserves outright into the system before the Christmas holiday and then forced to drain a portion of them after the holiday in January due to swings in currency demand.

"The Fed does not face that dilemma at this time of the year, and if the reserve needs warrant it, as we estimate they will, the Fed should purchase coupon securities at least by late February," the economists said.

It is also possible the Fed could extend the passes over a longer period of time rather than in just a few days as the Fed had traditionally done due to newly announced procedures the central bank said it would implement.
(( -- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury desk, 212-859-1663))
